name: What photos or details should I send before getting a trim repair estimate?
description: Send close-up and wide photos, plus any signs of leaks, rot, gaps, or peeling paint. That usually makes the estimate faster and more accurate.

mainEntity.name: What photos or details should I send before getting a trim repair estimate?

acceptedAnswer.text: Good evidence includes clear photos of the damage, a close-up of cracks or rot, wider shots showing where the trim sits, and notes about leaks, impact, or peeling paint. If you’re in Foxfield, Denver, or Parker, photos help a contractor judge whether the problem is isolated trim damage or part of a bigger moisture issue.
